messages.subject: sessionName
parts:
Hi Phil,

I have yet another question for you, this time regarding the new "sessionName" feature.
I'm hosting a mirtCAT based app on a shiny server (free version) and want to use mirtCAT to test multiple people simultaneously. In this regard, it makes absolute sense to assign a session name to each participant.
However, based on what I see in the documentation and from the error messages I get, it appears as though the session ID has to be defined as a variable and then passed along to the functions mirtCAT_preamble and createShinyGUI

An example could look like this:
mysession<-"example_ID"
mirtCAT_preable( ...,sessionName=mysession,...)
createShinyGUI(mysession, ...)

But like this, the session name is created as a global variable (created when the app is started for the first time) and not as a session variable (created when a participant connects to the app) as it is not inside the server-function/according mirtCAT function.

My questions thus are:
- Am I doing this wrong or is this the intended way? If so, how does the variable help to distinguish between sessions?
- Is there a way do create the sessionname as a local (i.e. session dependent) variable?

I would be really thankful for a quick response as the issue with the sessionname currently renders my CAT unusable...

Thanks in advance

Daniel

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: sessionName
parts:
Hi Daniel,

This is a confusing topic, so now would probably be a good time to discuss the issue. To answer your questions; no, the current approach is likely not what you want to ensure each session gets it's own session name (see the createSessionName() function for a better alternative). The better flow would be something more akin to :

mysession<-createSessionName()
mirtCAT_preable( ...,sessionName=mysession,...)
createShinyGUI(mysession, ...)

or what the current dev version of the package does (which is better yet)

mysession<-paste0(createSessionName(), Sys.time())
mirtCAT_preable( ...,sessionName=mysession,...)
createShinyGUI(mysession, ...)

The idea here is that each time a user logs into the server the uploaded server.R/ui.R files are effectively re-sourced into an R session, so in your example code everyone would get the same session name. This is bad, because if there are two instances of users logged in at the same time then the answers of one user actually influence the session of the other user since they are being written to the same isolated enviroment. Since I added the sessionName input this is avoided so long as a sufficiently random session name is provided to each user, which in the current CRAN version is a randomly generated character vector with 30 upper/lower cases (hence, the odds that any two session would ever share at the exact moment is extremely small). The dev version even goes one step further now to paste on the date/time the session started, so its now astronomically unlikely for two users to share the same session name simultaneously. 

The described problem is a limitation with the free version of shiny server, but this is a reasonably clever hack to avoid problems and allow single servers to be overloaded (the better solution would be to force individuals onto separate servers at the outset with the pro versions of shiny, or to create some type of virtual drives on the server to mimic the same behaviour). HTH with the understanding. 

Phil

messages.author: 0cc91f41491ff09e
messages.subject: Re: sessionName
parts:
Dear Phil,

thanks a lot for your quick reply and the information. However, I'm still a bit confused. If I understand the scoping rules of shiny regarding local and global variables correctly, the following would normally happen:
When the first user logs in, the R script is sourced. Once the app is running, however, the script is not re-sourced again, only the parts wrapped into the server and UI functions  are resourced. Thus, the first two lines of your code are not re-sourced for each participant and thus all get the same sessionname. Only when the app as a whole is stopped and another user later logs in, everything is going to be re-sourced.

I also implemented your code right now and two different computers, both running the same mirtCAT showan entangled behaviour. If I proceed in the CAT on one of them, I run into trouble in the other one and vice versa...

Thanks again for clarification

Best,

Daniel

messages.author: 0cc91f41491ff09e
messages.subject: Re: sessionName
parts:
Just as a follow up: I think one of the following alternatives would be suitable
  • Use the onstart parameter of the shinyApp function to define a sessionname or to call a function defining the session name. However, this would mean that the mirtCAT_preamble function must be called without session ID, as the preamble-Function is only executed once, when the first user logs in.
  • define a random session number within the server function of mirtCAT, when it is called. Like this, all participants get the same environment (same options in mirtCAT_preamble, etc, but would be in a different session of the program
Best,

Daniel
